title: Three Red Cards, a Nine-Minute Opener, and a Son Heung-min Substitution. Day 1 of the World Cup Had Everything.
excerpt: Mexico beat South Africa 2-0 in a fiery Azteca, South Korea came from behind to edge Czechia in Guadalajara, and three players saw red in the tournament's opening match.
body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup is underway — and the opening day delivered everything the tournament promised: drama, goals, red cards, and a comeback that reminded the world why football remains the planet's unifying obsession.

## Mexico 2-0 South Africa: The Host Sets the Tone

At a thundering Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, co-hosts Mexico dismantled South Africa in front of 87,000 fans who had barely settled from the spectacular opening ceremony. Julián Quiñones struck in the ninth minute after South Africa's goalkeeper misplayed a pass, picking off the ball and ripping a right-footed shot into the net. It was the first goal of the 2026 World Cup, and the crowd erupted.

The match turned ugly in the second half. South Africa's Sphephelo Sithole was shown a straight red card in the 50th minute for a last-man foul on Brian Gutiérrez, reducing Bafana Bafana to ten men. Veteran Raúl Jiménez — released by Fulham just days earlier — then headed home Roberto Alvarado's cross in the 67th minute for 2-0. It was Jiménez's first-ever World Cup goal across four tournaments.

But the drama was not over. Substitute Themba Zwane received a VAR-prompted red card for striking Alvarado, and Mexico's César Montes was dismissed in stoppage time. Three red cards in a single World Cup match — a wild marker for how referees intend to officiate this tournament.

"It's a moment I'll carry with me for the rest of my life," said Mexico midfielder Erik Lira. "The only thing I felt was that everything it took to get here had been worth it."

## South Korea 2-1 Czechia: The Comeback in Guadalajara

In the late kickoff at Estadio Guadalajara, South Korea came from behind to beat Czechia 2-1 in a match of stark contrasts. The first half was goalless despite South Korea dominating possession, with captain Son Heung-min creating five chances but failing to convert any.

Czechia struck first in the 59th minute through captain Ladislav Krejčí, who rose highest to head home from Vladimír Coufal's remarkable 35-metre throw-in — a slingshot set-piece tactic that defined the Czech approach.

South Korea responded within eight minutes. Hwang In-beom collected Lee Kang-in's through ball, faked a shot to beat two defenders, then chipped the ball over goalkeeper Matěj Kovář for a sublime equaliser. In the 80th minute, Hwang turned provider, delivering a cross from the right for substitute Oh Hyeon-gyu — who had replaced the misfiring Son — to finish from close range.

It was South Korea's first opening-game World Cup win since beating Greece in 2010, and their third consecutive defeat of a European opponent at the tournament.

## What NRIs in North America Should Watch Next

The tournament moves to Canadian and American soil on Friday. Canada hosts Bosnia and Herzegovina at BMO Field in Toronto at 3:00 PM ET — a historic first meeting between the two nations. For desi fans in the Greater Toronto Area, it is the first World Cup match ever played in Canada.

Then on Friday night, the United States faces Paraguay at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, at 6:00 PM PDT. NRIs in the Bay Area and Los Angeles can catch the action on FOX. Saturday brings Brazil vs Morocco at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey at 7:00 PM ET — a blockbuster pairing within driving distance of the massive desi communities in Edison, Jersey City, and Queens.

With 104 matches across 16 venues in three countries over the next five weeks, NRIs have never had a World Cup this close to home. The group stage alone runs through June 28, with knockout rounds beginning on June 29.
